title: Roberson's homomorphism-counting conjecture for proper minor-closed classes
statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a graph class that is proper, minor-closed, and union-closed. For graphs $G$ and $H$, write $G =_{\mathcal{M}} H$ when $\hom(K,G)=\hom(K,H)$ for every $K\in\mathcal{M}$. **Roberson's conjecture.** If $\mathcal{M}$ is a proper, minor-closed, and union-closed graph class, then there are non-isomorphic graphs $G$ and $H$ such that

$$
G =_{\mathcal{M}} H.
$$

This conjecture says that homomorphism counts from any such proper minor-closed class do not characterize graphs up to isomorphism. The source attributes it to Roberson; its resolution is not specified here.
source_name: Andrea Jiménez, Benjamin Moore, Daniel A. Quiroz and Youngho Yoo, “Homomorphism counting for immersion-closed classes is not isomorphism”, arXiv:2602.08738 (2026).
references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2023–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2601.18602](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18602), [arXiv:2304.07011](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.07011).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08738

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2026).
